podcast.title: London Indie Label (1993-Present)
podcast.body: Founded in London in 1993, this independent label struggled for the remainder of the 1990s, being marginalized as it and its roster were not part of the then-dominant Brit-pop scene. Despite challenges, it maintained enough credit and success to continue operating. "Domino, a London-based label founded in 1993 that just got out of the long for the rest of the decade."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: 2005 Breakthrough
podcast.body: Experienced a major breakthrough in 2005 when the Arctic Monkeys, a young and internet-savvy band, signed with them. This period also saw Franz Ferdinand, another Domino artist, achieve significant chart success, elevating the label's stature. "Their big break came in 2005 when a very young, very erudite, very internet-conscious band out of Sheffield came to their attention."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Arctic Monkeys Signing
podcast.body: Domino Records signed the Arctic Monkeys after the band had already amassed a massive online following through their innovative use of MySpace. This demonstrated a shift in the music industry, where bands could build significant fan bases and generate label bidding wars even after making their music freely available online. "By the time they signed with Domino Records, the band had a massive online following thanks to MySpace."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dominant British Independent Label
podcast.body: Domino is identified as one of the independent labels that dominate much of the British rock scene today. "much of the British rock scene is dominated by independent labels like Domino and Cooking Vinyl and Go Disks, Rough Trade, XL Recording and dozens and dozens more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Key Role in Classic Rock Revival
podcast.body: Domino Records was a very important record label during the classic rock revival movement. It is known for granting significant creative freedom to its artists, as exemplified by the contractual agreement with Arctic Monkeys. "Es una discográfica que fue muy importante en el todo este rival del rock clásico. Y realmente es una discográfica que da muchísima libertad creativa."

srcs.episode: Arctic Monkeys: Cómo nació un mito.

podcast.title: Limited Vinyl Release
podcast.body: Domino Records, referenced as "dígilo, mi no" in the transcript, undertook the release of a small, limited vinyl edition of the collaborative project between Björk and Dirty Projectors. This occurred approximately one year after the project's initial digital release, with the specific aim of generating additional funds for the marine conservation cause. "Lo digo todo, mi no, que es la discográfica que moda los transcernina, que moda los kilzas, y nada, muchísimos artistas indiquizos, una pequeña edición de este proyecto un poco para ayudar a recordar más dinero al proyecto."

srcs.episode: Björk y su curioso proyecto con los Dirty Proyectors

podcast.title: Signing of Arctic Monkeys
podcast.body: Domino Records won the bidding war for the Arctic Monkeys after their online demo phenomenon attracted numerous labels. Domino subsequently signed the band and oversaw the re-recording of many of their demos for their official debut album.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Support for Vinyl
podcast.body: Domino Records, Franz Ferdinand's main label, is praised for being "really cool" and understanding of artists' desires for physical media, particularly vinyl. They are described as "vinyl nuts" themselves. "Like, Domino is on main label and they're really cool with that stuff. They get it. They're vinyl nuts too."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
